instruction: Conduct a network speed test at speedtest.net, then store the report in ~/Downloads/network_test.txt.

metadata.explanation: Task requires running a speed test on speedtest.net and saving results to Downloads folder. The evaluator checks if network_test.txt in Downloads contains the essential metrics: Ping, Download, and Upload. This confirms the user completed the test and saved results to the specified location.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Binary scoring: 1.0 if all required keywords (Ping, Download, Upload) are present in the Downloads file, 0.0 otherwise

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly retrieves the file specified in instruction (~/Downloads/network_test.txt)
file_contains metric appropriately checks for presence of essential speedtest keywords
Expected values (Ping, Download, Upload) are semantically correct for speedtest.net results
Complete coverage: all three core speedtest metrics are verified
Data flow is correct: file retrieval -> content reading -> keyword verification
Minor issue: keyword matching is case-sensitive, could fail if speedtest.net outputs different capitalization (e.g., 'download' vs 'Download')
Minor issue: no verification of actual test data - user could create fake file with just these keywords
Minor issue: no timestamp validation to ensure test was recently run (unlike other speedtest tasks)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider case-insensitive keyword matching to handle different speedtest.net output formats
Consider adding regex patterns to verify actual numeric values are present (e.g., 'Download: \d+' instead of just 'Download')
Consider adding timestamp validation to ensure test was run recently, not using old results
